title: Describe an Object in an Exhibit

source.rights: 原创 AI 辅助虚构教学材料，尚待发布前独立审核。

instructions: Prepare briefly, then record your own answer. Aim for 90–120 seconds; this is a suggested target, not a minimum. Use at least six lesson words. To pass review, your answer’s transcript must contain at least 100 words, and the required audio and review evidence must be available. The reference and its audio are short language examples, not full-length demonstrations; create your own answer.
prompt: Describe an object you would include in a small community exhibit. Who made or chose it, what does it look like, and what story does it tell? Explain how visitors could learn about it. Aim to speak for 90–120 seconds and use at least six lesson words.
reference: I would include a ceramic bowl in a small community gallery. A local artist made it from clay, and the surface is blue and white. The object reminds her of meals with her grandfather, who taught her to prepare food. She has practiced pottery for several years, but this bowl was made last winter. I would put it in a simple display beside a short note about her story. A guide could explain how the bowl was made and invite visitors to ask questions. I would also include a piece of fabric from another neighbor, because the two objects show different kinds of craft. The collection could help people share memories without needing to buy anything.
